controversies/antinomian-controversies/q: Should the law be preached to those already justified by grace?
controversies/antinomian-controversies/t: The antinomian controversies: Wittenberg, Boston and Edinburgh
controversies/antinomian-controversies/s: Three times Protestants who agreed on justification by faith alone fought over the law’s place in the Christian life: Agricola against Melanchthon and Luther (1527–40), Anne Hutchinson against the Massachusetts ministers (1636–38) and the Marrow men against the Church of Scotland (1718–23).

We are justified wholly by Christ, and the Spirit himself bears witness that we are God’s children. When preachers drive believers back to the law and make them search their works for assurance, they quietly turn grace into a new covenant of works. Let Christ’s love be preached, and holiness will follow as fruit, not as fee.
Romans 6:14 and 7:4: believers are dead to the law
Repentance is worked by the gospel
Assurance by the Spirit’s witness, not by sanctification
Law and gospel with a third use

The law is holy, just and good. Without it sin is not known and grace is cheapened. It drives sinners to Christ and then, written on the heart by the Spirit, shows the redeemed how to love God and neighbour. To silence the law is to silence Scripture.
By the law is the knowledge of sin (Rom 3:20)
New covenant writes the law on the heart
Formula of Concord VI and Westminster 19
Marrow men: the free offer of Christ

We hold the Westminster Confession, but our church is confusing the covenants. Christ is to be freely offered to every sinner as he is, without first requiring a qualifying repentance; the believer is free from the law as a covenant of works yet bound to it as the rule of life in Christ’s hand.
Free offer of the gospel to all
Distinguishing law as covenant from law as rule
General Assembly saw universal-redemption and antinomian tendencies
controversies/antinomian-controversies/t: Agricola attacks Melanchthon’s Visitation Articles for teaching that repentance begins with the law.
The Augsburg Confession presents repentance as contrition and faith.
Luther publishes Against the Antinomians after a series of disputations; Agricola recants in 1540.
Formula of Concord Articles V–VI define law and gospel and the third use.
Puritans found Massachusetts Bay, stressing covenant and preparation for grace.
Anne Hutchinson tried at Newtown and banished; a synod condemns some eighty errors.
Westminster Confession defines the covenants and the law’s abiding use.
The Church of Scotland’s General Assembly condemns The Marrow of Modern Divinity.
Ebenezer Erskine and others form the Secession Church, partly in the Marrow tradition.
controversies/antinomian-controversies/r: Each episode ended with the official church rejecting the "antinomian" party (Formula of Concord 1577; Massachusetts synod 1637; General Assembly 1720), yet the protesters’ concerns about legalism and assurance were partly absorbed: Lutheranism kept a sharp law–gospel distinction, and the Marrow theology became influential in Scottish evangelicalism. The underlying question resurfaces in modern free-grace, lordship and "hyper-grace" debates.
controversies/antinomian-controversies/c: Clarified Lutheran and Reformed teaching on the law and sanctification.
Banishments that contributed to Rhode Island’s founding as a haven of dissent.
Provided vocabulary for later evangelical debates over assurance and holiness.
controversies/israel-and-the-church/ques: Has the Church replaced Israel, or does God’s covenant with the Jewish people endure?
controversies/israel-and-the-church/titl: Israel and the Church: supersession, distinction or enduring covenant?
controversies/israel-and-the-church/summ: Christians have long read themselves as the new or true Israel. After centuries of anti-Jewish teaching and the Shoah, churches have reconsidered: dispensationalists insist on a distinct future for Israel, post-supersessionists on an irrevocable Jewish covenant, Messianic Jews on Jewish identity in Christ, and fulfilment theologians on one people of God in the Messiah.
controversies/israel-and-the-church/side: Jesus is Israel’s Messiah and in him the promises to Abraham reach their goal: one new people of Jews and Gentiles. This is not hostility to Jews but the conviction that the Jewish Messiah is for Jews first. Contempt and violence were betrayals of Paul’s warning against Gentile pride, not the fruit of believing that Christ fulfils the Law.
One olive tree, one new man (Rom 11; Eph 2)
Israel’s titles applied to the church (1 Pet 2:9)
History of the teaching of contempt

God swore unconditional oaths to Abraham’s descendants about a land and a kingdom. If he could set those aside, how could the church trust his promises? Israel and the church are distinct, and Israel’s national restoration is still to come.
NT applies Israel texts to the church

Paul says God has not rejected his people and that his gifts and calling are irrevocable. After Auschwitz, Christians must repent not only of violence but of a theology that made the Jewish people obsolete. God’s faithfulness to Israel is the guarantee of his faithfulness to the church.

Yeshua is Israel’s Messiah, and believing in him makes us no less Jewish. The first church was Jewish; Jewish believers should keep their identity and bear witness among their people, while Gentiles join as Gentiles.
controversies/israel-and-the-church/time: The Jerusalem council frees Gentile believers from circumcision.
The Temple is destroyed; Christians read it as judgement and vindication.
After the Bar Kokhba revolt the Jerusalem church becomes wholly Gentile-led.
Marcion rejects the God of Israel and is expelled.
Lateran IV requires Jews to wear distinctive dress.
Expulsion of the Jews from Spain.
Scofield Reference Bible popularises the Israel–Church distinction.
Nostra Aetate repudiates the deicide charge and antisemitism.
Vatican document "The Gifts and the Calling of God Are Irrevocable" rejects institutional missions to Jews.
controversies/israel-and-the-church/reso: Open. Since 1945 virtually all major churches have condemned antisemitism and the deicide charge, and many have renounced punitive supersessionism; but they still differ on whether Jews need explicit faith in Christ, whether missions to Jews are appropriate, and on Israel’s land and future. Dialogue continues through bodies such as the International Council of Christians and Jews.
controversies/israel-and-the-church/cons: Catholic and Protestant revisions of catechesis and liturgy (e.g. the Good Friday prayer).
Christian Zionism as a political force, and Palestinian Christian critiques of it.
Renewed scholarship on Paul and Judaism.
controversies/galileo-affair/question: Must Scripture’s language about a fixed earth and moving sun be read as astronomy, and who decides?
controversies/galileo-affair/summary: From 1616 to 1633 Roman authorities judged Copernican heliocentrism contrary to Scripture and condemned Galileo; the case became the emblem of a “war” between science and religion, though historians now stress its theological, political and personal complexity.
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/0/nam: Scripture’s plain sense and Church authority
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/0/ste: For fifteen centuries the Fathers unanimously read Joshua 10, Psalm 93 and Ecclesiastes 1 as describing a stable earth and a moving sun. The Council of Trent forbids interpreting Scripture against the unanimous consent of the Fathers on matters of faith and morals. Copernicanism was an unproven hypothesis; Galileo’s tidal argument was weak and stellar parallax undetected. A layman should not reinterpret Scripture on his own authority. Cardinal Bellarmine himself conceded that if a true demonstration were found, the texts would need reinterpreting.
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/0/arg: Lack of decisive proof for the earth’s motion before parallax (1838)
Tycho Brahe’s geo-heliocentric model fitted the observations
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/0/cou: Astronomy is not a matter of faith and morals
Augustine himself warned against binding Scripture to disputable natural philosophy
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/1/ste: God is author of both Scripture and nature, and the two cannot truly contradict. Scripture speaks in ordinary language to teach salvation; it describes the sun “rising” as we all still do. As Augustine taught, Christians must not expose the faith to ridicule by making Scripture teach natural philosophy. Sense experience and necessary demonstrations should guide interpreters to the true meaning of the texts.
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/1/arg: Telescopic evidence: phases of Venus, Jupiter’s moons
Baronius: Scripture teaches how to go to heaven, not how the heavens go
controversies/galileo-affair/sides/1/cou: Galileo had no conclusive proof and overstated his tidal argument
He mocked the Pope’s argument in the Dialogue
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/0/: Copernicus’ On the Revolutions published, dedicated to Pope Paul III.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/1/: Trent forbids interpreting Scripture contrary to the unanimous consent of the Fathers.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/2/: Galileo’s Starry Messenger reports Jupiter’s moons.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/3/: Letter to the Grand Duchess Christina.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/4/: The Index suspends Copernicus’ book “until corrected”; Bellarmine admonishes Galileo.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/5/: Galileo tried, made to abjure, sentenced to house arrest.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/6/: Holy Office allows printing of books teaching the earth’s motion.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/7/: Copernican works dropped from the Index.
controversies/galileo-affair/timeline/8/: John Paul II receives the commission’s report and acknowledges the judges’ error.
controversies/galileo-affair/resolution/: Heliocentrism became universally accepted, and the Catholic Church gradually withdrew its prohibitions (1757-1835) and in 1992 acknowledged that Galileo’s judges erred. Historians debate whether the affair was a clash of science and religion at all, or chiefly of competing authorities, personalities and Counter-Reformation politics.
controversies/galileo-affair/consequence: Became the founding myth of the “warfare thesis” (Draper 1874, White 1896), now largely rejected by historians of science.
Encouraged the principle, shared by most churches, that Scripture is not a textbook of natural science.
Shaped later Catholic caution and the 1950 Humani Generis approach to evolution.
controversies/creation-evolution-debate/: Is the evolutionary history of life compatible with the Christian doctrine of creation, Adam and the fall?

Since 1859 Christians have divided over evolution: many accepted it as God’s method, others rejected Darwinism’s apparent exclusion of design, and from 1961 a revived young-earth creationism made the issue a marker of evangelical identity, with intelligent design as a third party.

Genesis is God’s eyewitness account, and Jesus treated it as history. If death and suffering existed for millions of years before Adam, then death is not the wages of sin, and the cross loses its context. The age of the earth is not observed but inferred from assumptions; Christians should start from God’s Word, not from naturalistic science.
Plain reading of Genesis and Exodus 20:11
Convergent scientific evidence for deep time and common descent
Old-earth views held by many 19th-century conservatives

God is not a rival to natural processes but their Creator and sustainer. The evidence for common descent is as strong as for any scientific theory. Genesis proclaims that the one God made a good world and called humanity to bear his image — truths untouched by how long or by what means. Making Christianity depend on a young earth sets an unnecessary stumbling block before inquirers.
Augustine’s warning against embarrassing the faith
Ancient Near Eastern genre of Genesis 1
Threatens historical Adam and the fall
Makes God use suffering and death as creative tools
Concedes too much to naturalism (ID critique)

Whatever the age of the earth, the information in DNA and the molecular machines of the cell bear the hallmarks of mind. Science should be free to follow the evidence to design rather than ruling it out by methodological naturalism.
Charles Hodge: “What is Darwinism? It is atheism.”
Scofield Reference Bible promotes the gap theory.
The Fundamentals include essays open to an old earth and limited evolution.
Humani Generis allows Catholic study of human bodily evolution.
The Genesis Flood revives flood geology.
Behe’s Darwin’s Black Box; John Paul II calls evolution more than a hypothesis.
Kitzmiller v. Dover rules against teaching ID.

Unresolved. Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican and mainline Protestant teaching generally accepts evolution under providence; a large share of evangelicals, Pentecostals and many Global South Christians hold young-earth or old-earth creationism; intelligent design persists as a minority intellectual movement.
Shaped American fundamentalism and its institutions after Scopes.
Generated creation museums, curricula and court cases.
Produced new theological work on human origins, original sin and animal suffering.
Remains a frequent factor in young people’s reported loss of faith and in scientists’ perception of Christianity.
